newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC members optimistic after coffee export talks.
newsitem.headline: ACPC members optimistic after coffee export talks.

text.p: Talks among members of Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) were proceeding well, and producers hoped to have a final document ready in the early afternoon, officials said after breaking for lunch.
"Things are going well, we have 90 percent of the document already agreed," Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, told reporters.
Producers are meeting to discuss an African proposal to cut member exports further in the first half of this year.
Earlier today, the Ugandan Trade and Industry Minister told Reuters that producers had alrewady agreed on a minimum cut of not less than one million 60-kg bags.
Today, observers said the final amount may be nearer to 1.5 million, including 500,000 bags of arabica divided between Brazil and Colombia.
Producer delegates uniformly declined to comment on a possible cut after this morning's session but were unanimously optimistic.
"We are in the final stage, we are talking about the future," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"We made advances and after lunch I think we will have only another hour of discussion," said ACPC president Rubens Barbosa.
